instructions: Rinse the lentils in a sieve. Peel 1 carrot and dice it small.

Put the lentils, carrot, bay leaf, 1/2 tsp of the salt and 3 cups of water in a saucepan. Bring it to a boil over high heat, then turn it to medium-low and simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes. Start checking at 18 minutes. They're done when they're tender but still hold their shape.
Meanwhile, mince the shallot and the garlic. In a large bowl, whisk them with the mustard, vinegar, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper. Slowly whisk in the olive oil.
Drain the lentils and take out the bay leaf. Add the warm lentils to the dressing and toss. Do this while they're warm so they take up the dressing.
Leave the salad for 15 minutes, until it's at room temperature. Chop 1/4 cup of parsley and stir it in.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt, or a splash of the vinegar.
It keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days. Stir before you pack a portion and serve it cold or at room temperature.
method_notes: No version showed 20 or more ratings, so this is a fallback; the lead is Full of Plants (4.75 from 4 votes, visible rating), with America's Test Kitchen at 4 stars from 3 ratings. All agree on French green lentils tossed warm in a sharp vinaigrette with fresh parsley. The lead uses balsamic and nutritional yeast; I used a Dijon and red wine vinegar dressing, as the dish names, and added a small diced carrot cooked with the lentils and a bay leaf, as ATK does. Storage of 4 days comes from the lead.
